action.body: In our recent investigation of rhythmic structures, we explored whether information-theoretic entropy could serve as a reliable metric for quantifying syncopation and complexity. The findings suggest that while entropy provides a rigorous framework for non-isochronous rhythms, the challenge of non-stationarity—where statistical properties change over time—remains significant. Human rhythm perception is elastic and adaptive; mathematical models must be equally resilient. Our analysis highlights that applying these tools to music requires a careful separation of signal from noise to avoid overstating complexity.
action.lede: How do we measure the 'feeling' of a complex rhythm? Information theory offers a path, but warns of the traps in non-stationarity.
action.lens: Math can define a rhythm's complexity, but it cannot hear the groove. We must be careful not to conflate the measure of uncertainty with the experience of musical time.
action.reason: Synthesis of music rhythm research via information theory is a meaningful milestone.
action.title: Entropy and Rhythmic Complexity
